pagerduty-bot: PagerDuty: Triggered ONCALL_SCHEDULE (incident #INC-9742). Auto-escalation in 5m if not acknowledged.

oncall-jordan: acked — looking

oncall-jordan: seeing sustained backlog on /inference-request-queue: backlog: 34620, processing rate down 60% vs baseline. 95p latency 2s -> 14s. Some clients reporting 503s.

oncall-jordan: quick checks: autoscaler metrics show controllers failing to launch new pods: "scale-up rejected: nodepool-quota-exceeded" in cluster events.

oncall-jordan: running: ```kubectl get hpa -n inference inference-autoscaler -o yaml``` to confirm; grabbing nodepool status now.

oncall-jordan: cluster events snippet: "FailedCreatePod: insufficient quota: nodeQuota: requested 4, available 0"

oncall-jordan: manual scale attempt: ```kubectl scale deploy/inference-worker --replicas=40 -n inference``` -> pods stuck Pending with reason: "0/0 nodes available"

oncall-jordan: tagging eng-platform for quota lift / temporary spot increase @eng-platform

maya: on it — checking cloud console for recent quota usage and outstanding node pool requests. I see a recent scheduled maintenance last night that drained a host pool (pool-a), autoscaler couldn't provision to pool-b because taints mismatch.

eli: re: taints — I pushed a change last week to default node affinity to avoid noisy noisy-gpu hosts. Looks like the new node pool in us-west-2 doesn't match affinity rules. Rolling a config with relaxed tolerations now (prelim patch): ```kubectl patch daemonset node-affinity-controller -n infra --type='json' -p='[ {"op": "replace", "path": "/spec/template/spec/tolerations", "value": [{"key":"dedicated","operator":"Exists","effect":"NoSchedule"},{"operator":"Exists","effect":"NoExecute"}] } ]'```

oncall-jordan: good — if we relax tolerations new nodes should accept pods. ETA?

eli: patch applied, cloud autoscaler logs now show node requests in flight. Starting to provision 8 nodes.

ops-bot: system: temporary routing policy applied: route high-latency traffic to fallback-compact-models to reduce token-time per request. Traffic shift 20% for canary.

oncall-jordan: initiating manual queue drain by increasing worker replicas after nodes come up. Also enabling prefix-caching for hot keys to reduce re-compute. Command: ```sh
# increase workers gradually to avoid cold-start storm
kubectl scale deploy/inference-worker -n inference --replicas=80
```

oncall-jordan: customer impact: some enterprise customers seeing 30-50% error spikes on batch endpoints; public API rate-limited to keep system stable. Notifying support to open inbound tickets.

maya: cloud quota team confirmed temporary quota bump ( +12 nodes) granted, expected nodes ready in ~6m. Also fixing taint mismatch in pool-b to accept GPU workloads.

oncall-jordan: monitoring: backlog halved to ~17k after first 8 nodes; 95p latency down to 6s. Error rate dropping but still above baseline.

oncall-jordan: marking incident SEV=2 for now, will escalate if customer SLA breaches observed.

eli: FYI, autoscaler controller logs show a race where new node pools are created but node labels mismatch model-selector; I'll follow up with a PR to include model-selector labels in the pool bootstrap.

ops-bot: pd-note: Incident #INC-9742 acknowledged by oncall-jordan. Escalation to eng-platform requested.

eng-platform: adding nodepool-label sync task and standing by to approve additional capacity. Also initiating hotfix to autoscaler policy to prefer existing taint-compatible pools when scaling.

oncall-jordan: handoff plan: I'll stay on until backlog <5k and 95p latency <2s. If still above thresholds at +60m, escalate to SRE lead for paging. Handoff to sophia at 3287654380.

sophia: taking over at handoff. Please drop any follow-ups here and brief me on current mitigation steps.

oncall-jordan: brief: 1) quota bump in progress (12 nodes) 2) toleration patch applied 3) manual replica scale to 80 in flight 4) traffic shift 20% to compact models 5) support notified of customer impact 6) autoscaler race condition noted (eli) — follow-up PR queued.

sophia: thanks — I'll monitor dashboards and coordinate postmortem. Creating an incident doc and linking PD ticket. If queue starts climbing again, we'll trigger emergency surge policy (disable canary traffic + increase replica cap to 200)

oncall-jordan: logs attached to PD: https://redwood.slack/links/INC-9742/logs (internal)
